preamble: Debuccalization of the alveolar fricative [s] to a glottal stop [ʔ] removes the oral constriction and leaves only glottal closure. Most Caribbean and other lowland Spanish dialects weaken coda /s/ to [h] or delete it. Puerto Rican Spanish has also developed a glottal-stop variant of word-final /s/. It was first reported before vowels (las islas [laʔ ˈislas]) and later found before consonants as well. The variant is often linked to contact with English. A Lancaster, Pennsylvania study found it among young Puerto Rican speakers but not among Cuban or Dominican speakers.

examples.note: Word-final /s/ before a vowel; this is the context where the glottal variant was first described.
Pre-consonantal glottal realization of /s/, reported more recently.
A spectrogram from a Puerto Rican speaker in Lancaster, Pennsylvania shows the glottal closure before hablo.

sources: Valentín-Márquez, W. (2022). A comparative study of /s/ in Puerto Rican Spanish and the Cuban and Dominican dialects. Borealis 11(2). https://doi.org/10.7557/1.11.2.6424
Mohamed, S. & Muntendam, A. (2020). The use of the glottal stop as a variant of /s/ in Puerto Rican Spanish. Studies in Hispanic and Lusophone Linguistics. https://doi.org/10.1515/shll-2020-2035
context: Word-final /s/, before vowels and consonants, in Puerto Rican Spanish
